raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes #8990

## Summary

The change has three parts:

1. **Fix three device-agnostic defects in the `zero_quantized_nontrainable_weights` path** (int8 storage of frozen weights, used by LoRA + ZeRO-3).
   - Quantize the partition only after the real weights have been copied in. Previously the code quantized an uninitialized buffer and then overwrote it with a dtype-cast copy of fp16/bf16 weights, truncating values in (-1, 1) to zero in the int8 storage. The model silently output zeros and the loss never moved.
   - Assign the quantizer on the `Init` class so the no-gather handles used on single-rank runs can dequantize (`AttributeError: type object 'Init' has no attribute 'quantizer_module'`).
   - In coalesced buckets whose params carry their own quantized storage, dequantize each param with its own scale and re-quantize the bucket uniformly. A flat dequantize with concatenated per-param scales computes a wrong `elems_per_group` whenever group counts differ (silent on CUDA, divisibility assertion on NPU). Also cast the fetched weights to `param.dtype`, not the int8 storage dtype. The per-param dequantize stays in the fp16 wire dtype because a quantized bucket may mix parameter dtypes, and fully padded partitions are zeroed before the bucket re-quantize so uninitialized padding cannot feed the shared group scale.

2. **Reject CPU parameter offload with this flag at init**, because the quantizer runs on the accelerator and the partition would not stay on the CPU. NVMe parameter offload is left unquantized with a warning.

3. **Extend `NPUQuantizer` to the int4/asymmetric contract and round half to even**, matching the CUDA kernel (`__float2int_rn`). `quantize` now packs int4 two per byte; `dequantize` accepts N-D packed inputs and asymmetric params; the reference test in `tests/unit/ops/quantizer/test_quantize.py` covers int8/int4, symmetric/asymmetric. Production hpZ/qgZ continue to use symmetric int8. The half-to-even change is adapted from #8764 (author: vineethsaivs).

## Files changed

- `deepspeed/runtime/zero/partition_parameters.py` (+68/-28)
- `op_builder/npu/quantizer.py` (+87/-36)
- `tests/unit/ops/quantizer/test_quantize.py` (+50)
- `tests/unit/v1/zero/test_quantized_nontrainable.py` (new, +157)

## Motivation

`zero_quantized_nontrainable_weights` is the option that makes LoRA fine-tuning cheap in ZeRO-3: frozen base weights are stored as int8 and dequantized on fetch. On master the option is effectively unusable:

- Frozen weights are all zeros in storage, with a scale derived from uninitialized memory. Training runs, the loss is `mean(label**2)`, and gradients are zero -- no error is raised. On NPU the same path later fails even harder: a second fetch leaks int8 storage into matmul and raises `Tensor mat2 not implemented for DT_INT8`.
- Single-rank runs crash immediately.
- Multi-parameter buckets either corrupt values or assert, depending on backend.

The rounding change addresses a separate but related accuracy issue in the same quantizer: truncation biases int4 qgZ gradients low (sum ~0.85 of the exact value in a 2x2 CPU simulation), while the CUDA kernel rounds.

## Testing

- NPU: Ascend 910B4, CANN 8.5.1, torch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post7, transformers 4.57.6, peft 0.20.0.
- GPU: 2x A100-SXM4-80GB (cards 4/5), driver 580.126.16, torch 2.14.1+cu126, CUDA 12.6 (nvcc 12.4), Python 3.10.22, transformers 4.57.6, peft 0.21.2.

The end-to-end scripts live outside the repository. They are device-agnostic through `get_accelerator()` and were run unchanged on both devices.

### In-repo regression test

`tests/unit/v1/zero/test_quantized_nontrainable.py` (new, world sizes 1 and 2):

- Branch, NPU: `pytest tests/unit/v1/zero/test_quantized_nontrainable.py -q --forked` -> 2 passed (both world sizes; storage/repartition and CPU-offload rejection), 89.30s.
- Branch, GPU: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5 pytest tests/unit/v1/zero/test_quantized_nontrainable.py -q --forked` -> 2 passed (A100-SXM4-80GB, torch 2.14.1+cu126, world sizes 1 and 2), 27.38s.
- The storage/repartition case fails on master with `AssertionError: quantized storage is all zeros`.
- Coverage: init storage and dequantization inside the group-scale bound; forward output against a plain-torch reference; the coalesced-bucket fetch after backward; the ZeRO-3 state-dict load through `load_module_state_dict(..., fetch_z3_params=True)` (the repartition path used when loading a checkpoint); the single-rank no-gather path; and the CPU-offload rejection. The test skips when the quantizer op is unavailable.
- It lives under `tests/unit/v1`, so the PR-level v1 workflow selects it. `python ci/tests_fetcher.py --base origin/master` returns mode `all` (because `op_builder/npu/quantizer.py` is a shared file) and selects `tests/unit/v1`, which includes the new test.

### Unit tests

| Test | NPU | GPU |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/unit/v1/zero/test_quantized_nontrainable.py` | 2 passed (both world sizes; CPU-offload rejection included) | 2 passed (A100-SXM4-80GB; both world sizes) |
| `tests/unit/checkpoint/test_zero_affine.py` | 27 passed | 27 passed (4 GPUs; 2 GPUs skip 4 AutoTP cases) |
| `tests/unit/ops/quantizer/test_quantize.py` | 242 passed (full matrix, 27.47s) | 242 passed (full matrix, 4.78s) |
| `test_zeropp.py::TestZeroPPConfigSweep` (hpZ, 4 ranks) | 9 passed (4 cards) | 9 passed |
| `test_zero_autocast_mixed_dtype.py` + `test_zero_allreduce_fetch_params.py` + non-sequential `test_zeropp.py` | 8 passed | 8 passed |

Notes on `test_quantize.py`:

- Every case is marked `inference_ops`, so `pytest.ini` deselects them when the command is run verbatim; use `-m "inference_ops or not inference_ops"`.
- The file is device-agnostic and collects on NPU. `NPUQuantizer.quantize` now covers int4 (two per byte) and asymmetric scale+zero point, so the full 242-case matrix runs on NPU as well as CUDA.
- The new rounding cases use the accelerator-resolved `QuantizerBuilder` (`quantize` for int8, `swizzle_quant` for int4), so they run against CUDA or NPU without importing a platform module.
- CUDA's reciprocal scale differs from the torch reference by 1-2 ULP. The test compares scales with a small tolerance and checks the dequantized output bitwise against the kernel's own params; a truncate-vs-round change still changes `q` and fails.
- CI note: the `test_quantize.py` cases carry `inference_ops`. `nv-inference` runs that marker, but its PR path filter does not include `op_builder/npu/quantizer.py` or `tests/unit/ops/quantizer/**`; the v1 PR workflow collects only `tests/unit/v1`. They therefore run manually/nightly, not in this PR's v1 job. The v1 regression test above is the PR-blocking one.

`pre-commit` passes on all changed files except the local `flake8` hook, which fails with `AttributeError: module 'ast' has no attribute 'Str'` (tool/Python incompatibility, unrelated to the change).

### Before / after on master

Observable failure modes on master versus this branch; each row maps to one defect.

| Check | master | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regression test (storage case) | fails: `quantized storage is all zeros` | passes |
| Qwen3-0.6B frozen storage | 0% non-zero | 98.8% non-zero |
| Single rank | `AttributeError: type object 'Init' has no attribute 'quantizer_module'` | passes |
| Multi-param coalesced bucket | int8 cast error on NPU / wrong group sizes on CUDA | passes |

### Real-model training, GPU vs NPU

Qwen3 models + PEFT LoRA (r=8 on q/k/v/o), 2 ranks, 20 steps on a fixed text batch. Both devices build the model from config only (`--random-init`, seed 0), so no weights need to be downloaded; loss is comparable across devices but not to a pretrained model.

| Model | Arm | Init GPU / NPU (MiB/rank) | Peak GPU / NPU (MiB/rank) | Frozen storage (B/rank) | Loss GPU | Loss NPU |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B (596.0M frozen) | quantized | 1,251 / 1,308 | 3,468 / 3,579 | 298,273,412 | 12.418 -> 6.359 | 12.257 -> 6.044 |
| | fp16 control | 1,557 / 1,603 | 3,774 / 3,871 | 596,049,920 | 12.422 -> 6.247 | 12.262 -> 5.880 |
| Qwen3-1.7B (1,720.6M frozen) | quantized | 1,789 / 1,845 | 5,041 / 6,207 | 860,955,972 | 12.249 -> 0.042 | 12.230 -> 0.036 |
| | fp16 control | 2,608 / 2,608 | 5,864 / 5,989 | 1,720,574,976 | 12.236 -> 0.027 | 12.246 -> 0.039 |
| Qwen3-4B (4,022.5M frozen) | quantized | 2,921 / 2,951 | 7,091 / 8,534 | 2,012,639,940 | 12.881 -> 0.024 | 12.302 -> 0.010 |
| | fp16 control | 4,839 / 4,840 | 9,047 / 9,102 | 4,022,468,096 | 12.871 -> 0.016 | 12.319 -> 0.009 |

- All quantized runs: 310/310 int8 partitions on 0.6B and 1.7B, 398/398 on 4B, 98.8% non-zero on both devices.
- Init-allocated savings (quantized vs control): GPU 306 / 819 / 1,918 MiB, NPU 295 / 763 / 1,889 MiB. The frozen storage itself halves at every size, and the byte counts are identical across devices.
- Training peak is lower with quantization in every GPU run. On NPU the 1.7B peak is 218 MiB higher (6,207 vs 5,989) because peak includes the fp16 all-gather buffers and bucket re-quantize transients; treat peak as workload-dependent, and init-allocated/storage as the stable savings.
- 0.6B checkpoint (8 steps): GPU replay 8.1402, NPU replay 8.1354 (step 7 repeats step 5); both ALL PASS. Frozen storage is zeroed before the load, so the continuation proves restoration.
- The coalesced-bucket re-quantize path runs repeatedly (quantize counter +9 per step on 0.6B, +42 per step on 1.7B).

The NPU also ran the same three models with pretrained weights: init allocated 1,307 / 1,600, 1,845 / 2,608 and 2,952 / 4,840 MiB, identical frozen storage, and losses 0.932 -> 0.021 / 0.863 -> 0.001 / 0.718 -> 0.003 (control 0.934 -> 0.015 / 0.883 -> 0.000 / 0.705 -> 0.001). The storage and memory numbers agree with the random-init runs within 1-8 MiB.

### Not tested

- Pretrained weights on GPU: the GPU real-model runs use random-init weights. Storage and memory metrics match the NPU pretrained-weight runs; loss values are not comparable to a pretrained model.
- bf16 and fp32 storage: not validated. `stage3.quantize_nontrainable_params()` still asserts fp16, so the post-init bf16 workflow remains out of scope.
- NVMe parameter offload: not exercised by the regression test; quantization is skipped with a warning.
- Padding: the in-repo test does not construct partial or fully padded partitions; those audit fixes are validated by inspection and the end-to-end runs, not by a targeted regression case.
- `stage3.quantize_nontrainable_params()` (the post-init re-quantize workflow) is not exercised by the in-repo test.
- hpZ `ds_secondary_tensor` (`_partition_param_sec`) has no targeted quantization test; the hpZ suites cover the primary path.
- Full `save_checkpoint`/`load_checkpoint` round trip is covered by the external Qwen3 script; the in-repo test uses `load_module_state_dict(..., fetch_z3_params=True)`.
- Cross-world-size checkpoint loading, TP/PP, and accelerators other than A100 and 910B4.

## Offload behavior

- CPU parameter offload + `zero_quantized_nontrainable_weights`: rejected at init with `NotImplementedError`; the in-repo regression test covers this path. The quantizer runs on the accelerator, so the partition would not stay on the CPU.
- NVMe parameter offload: quantization is skipped and a warning is emitted; frozen partitions keep their unquantized dtype. This combination is not exercised by the regression test.

## Compatibility and risk

- No API, config, or checkpoint format change.
- `zero_quantized_nontrainable_weights` users on CUDA get correct storage instead of zeros; single-rank and multi-param buckets start working.
- hpZ (`zero_quantized_weights`), autocast communication and the general fetch path are unchanged when the flag is off; the regression suites above pass.
- CPU offload with the flag now fails early instead of silently moving the storage to the accelerator; NVMe offload skips quantization with a warning.
- Existing quantized checkpoints: storage produced by the old code was all zeros and unusable, so no compatible checkpoint exists to preserve.

## Notes for review

- The three storage defects are described in #8990.
- The chosen fix keeps the existing wire format and quantizer. The bucket path mirrors the on-the-fly hpZ bucket logic that is already exercised in production.
- AI assistance was used to develop this change and its test harness. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the GPU validation above.
- Standalone reproducers and verification scripts can be provided on request; they live outside the repository (hardware-specific test harness).

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit` on all changed files (only the local `flake8` tool incompatibility remains)
- [x] In-repo regression test (fails on master; 2 cases pass on NPU and A100 at world sizes 1 and 2)
- [x] Quantizer contract tests (int8/int4, symmetric/asymmetric) in `tests/unit/ops/quantizer/test_quantize.py`
- [x] End-to-end validation of the storage fix on NPU (1 and 2 ranks) and CUDA (A100, 1 and 2 ranks)
- [x] Multi-rank LoRA + ZeRO-3 training on Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B/4B (pretrained weights on NPU, random-init weights on GPU)
- [x] CUDA hardware validation (A100: unit tests, Qwen3 real-model runs)
- [x] Throughput comparison for Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B (A100 steady-state and NPU incl warmup)

+        self.h = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.randn(32, 512) * 0.02)
+        self.w1.requires_grad_(False)
+        self.w2.requires_grad_(False)
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        return F.linear(F.linear(x, self.w1), self.w2) @ self.h.t()
+
+
+def _reference(w1, w2, h, x):
+    return F.linear(F.linear(x, w1), w2) @ h.t()
+
+
+def _config(world_size):
+    return {
+        "train_batch_size": 8 * world_size,
+        "train_micro_batch_size_per_gpu": 8,
+        "steps_per_print": 1,
+        "fp16": {
+            "enabled": True,
+            "initial_scale_power": 8,
+        },
+        "optimizer": {
+            "type": "Adam",
+            "params": {
+                "lr": 1e-3
+            },
+        },
+        "zero_optimization": {
+            "stage": 3,
+            "zero_quantized_nontrainable_weights": True,
+            "stage3_prefetch_bucket_size": 1e9,
+        },
+    }
+
+
+def _check_quantized_partition(param, full_weight, rank):
+    q = param.ds_tensor.data
+    scale = param.ds_tensor.ds_quant_scale
+    assert q.dtype == torch.int8
+    assert (q != 0).any(), "quantized storage is all zeros"
+
+    groups = scale.numel()
+    elems = q.numel() // groups
+    dequantized = q.view(groups, elems).float() * scale.view(groups, 1)
+    start = rank * q.numel()
+    expected = full_weight.reshape(-1)[start:start + q.numel()].float().view(groups, elems)
+    # One stored scale is one quantization step; allow one step of slack.
+    bound = scale.view(groups, 1).expand(groups, elems) * 1.05
+    assert torch.all((dequantized - expected).abs() <= bound)
+
+
+class TestZeroQuantizedNontrainableWeights(DistributedTest):
+    world_size = [1, 2]
+
+    def test_cpu_offload_is_rejected(self):
+        if not _QUANTIZER_AVAILABLE:
+            pytest.skip("quantizer op is not available")
+        if not get_accelerator().is_fp16_supported():
+            pytest.skip("requires fp16 support")
+
+        world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
+        device = get_accelerator().current_device_name()
+        model = _QuantizedLeaf().half().to(device)
+        config = _config(world_size)
+        config["zero_optimization"]["offload_param"] = {"device": "cpu"}
+
+        with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match="CPU parameter offload"):
+            deepspeed.initialize(model=model, model_parameters=model.parameters(), config=config)
+
+    def test_storage_forward_and_repartition(self):
+        if not _QUANTIZER_AVAILABLE:
+            pytest.skip("quantizer op is not available")
+        if not get_accelerator().is_fp16_supported():
+            pytest.skip("requires fp16 support")
+
+        world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
+        rank = dist.get_rank()
+        device = get_accelerator().current_device_name()
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        model = _QuantizedLeaf().half().to(device)
+        initial = {name: p.detach().clone() for name, p in model.named_parameters()}
+        inputs = torch.randn(8, 768, device=device).half()
+        label = torch.randn(8, 32, device=device).half()
+
+        engine, *_ = deepspeed.initialize(model=model, model_parameters=model.parameters(), config=_config(world_size))
+        try:
+            for name in ("w1", "w2"):
+                _check_quantized_partition(getattr(model, name), initial[name], rank)
+
+            # Load while the params are still NOT_AVAILABLE, so this goes through
+            # fetch -> load -> repartition and re-quantizes the storage.
+            torch.manual_seed(42)
+            new_state = {
+                "w1": (torch.randn(1024, 768, device=device) * 0.02).half(),
+                "w2": (torch.randn(512, 1024, device=device) * 0.02).half(),
+                "h": (torch.randn(32, 512, device=device) * 0.02).half(),
+            }
+            engine.load_module_state_dict({"module": new_state}, fetch_z3_params=True)
+            for name in ("w1", "w2"):
+                _check_quantized_partition(getattr(model, name), new_state[name], rank)
+
+            ref_out = _reference(new_state["w1"], new_state["w2"], new_state["h"], inputs)
+            out = engine(inputs)
+            torch_assert_close(out, ref_out, rtol=1e-2, atol=_FORWARD_TOL)
+
+            loss = F.mse_loss(out, label)
+            engine.backward(loss)
+
+            # A fetch after backward goes through the coalesced bucket path.
+            out_after_backward = engine(inputs)
+            torch_assert_close(out_after_backward, ref_out, rtol=1e-2, atol=_FORWARD_TOL)
+
+            h_before = model.h.detach().clone()
+            engine.step()
+            out_after_step = engine(inputs)
+            updated_h = model.h.detach().clone()
+            assert not torch.equal(updated_h, h_before)
+            torch_assert_close(out_after_step,
+                               _reference(new_state["w1"], new_state["w2"], updated_h, inputs),
+                               rtol=1e-2,
+                               atol=_FORWARD_TOL)
+        finally:
+            engine.destroy()
